recipes.subject: asciinema-player accepts application/octet-stream — the mime is NOT a blocker
recipes.observed: Trial A (same-origin, content-type application/octet-stream): hasBpDev=true, termLen=1908 — the v3 cast decoded and painted 'bp dev' into .ap-term. Trial D (cross-origin, CORRECT application/json mime, no ACAO): hasBpDev=false. Mime is irrelevant in both directions; ACAO is the only variable that moves the outcome.

recipes.subject: the exact live media-serve shape fails cross-origin purely on the missing ACAO header
recipes.observed: Replicated live headers (content-type: application/octet-stream; x-content-type-options: nosniff; content-disposition: inline). WITHOUT ACAO: fetch THREW 'Failed to fetch', console 'blocked by CORS policy: No Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is present', playsRealContent=false. WITH access-control-allow-origin:* and byte-identical everything else: playsRealContent=true, termLen=445. nosniff and content-disposition:inline are harmless.

recipes.subject: div.ap-player is a FALSE-POSITIVE assertion — it mounts even on total load failure
recipes.observed: ap-player=1 in BOTH the passing and the CORS-failing trial; .ap-control-bar present in both. asciinema-player mounts its shell synchronously and fetches the cast afterwards. hydratePortableDoc likewise returns {asciicast:1} on total failure — its return value counts MOUNTS, not successful loads. Any media gate must assert on .ap-term innerText (or absence of .ap-overlay-error), never on player presence or the hydrate count.

recipes.subject: reader-visible failure surface when the cast 404s/CORS-fails is a bare 💥 emoji
recipes.observed: div.ap-overlay-error innerText == '💥' — no message, no alt text, no kilde. A bordered box with an emoji and the figcaption below it. Bears directly on the komposisjon no-empty-box law for media fallbacks.

recipes.subject: the media blob route is on pipe_through(:api), which has no PublicCors — the defect is upstream, not in jarl
recipes.rerun: git -C /Users/frikkjarl/Documents/GitHub/barkpark show origin/main:api/lib/barkpark_web/router.ex | awk 'NR>=2054 && NR<=2061' ; git -C /Users/frikkjarl/Documents/GitHub/barkpark show origin/main:api/lib/barkpark_web/router.ex | awk '/^  pipeline :api do/,/^  end/'
recipes.observed: router.ex:2054 scope "/media" -> pipe_through(:api); :2060 get("/files/*path", MediaController, :serve). pipeline :api = AcceptBarkparkVendor, accepts json, ApiSecurityHeaders, ErrorEnvelopeNegotiation, RateLimit, OptionalToken, AssignDefaultScope, TenantLogMetadata — NO PublicCors. pipeline :public_api (:646) = accepts json + ApiSecurityHeaders + PublicCors. The plug already exists; the media serve route simply is not on it.

recipes.subject: .cast files are classified non-dangerous, so they serve inline as octet-stream
recipes.observed: @dangerous_mimes covers svg/html/xml/js only; serve_content_type/1 passes everything else through unchanged; disposition/1 returns "inline" for non-dangerous. MIME.from_path(".cast") yields application/octet-stream. So the live shape is octet-stream + inline + nosniff — proven harmless above. NO mime fix is needed on the upload path.

recipes.subject: the figure block DOES wrap an arbitrary child block with a caption — it is the kilde carrier
recipes.observed: var figure = (b) => { const child = b.child; const caption = str(b.caption); const childHtml = isMap(child) ? renderBlock2(child) : ""; return `` }. Verified live: figure{child:image} rendered . The image block's missing caption field needs NO engine change — wrap it in figure. Bonus: figcaptionInner auto-bolds a leading 'Figure N.' token.

recipes.subject: the asciicast player theme is hardcoded dark-only in the vendored client
recipes.observed: player.create(src, el, { fit:'width', poster:'npt:0:1', idleTimeLimit:2, theme:'asciinema' }) — literal, no light/dark branch, unlike hydrateMermaid which calls activeMermaidTheme(). Confirms the digest claim. Rendered class on the mounted node: 'asciinema-player-theme-asciinema'. Engine change + one re-vendor.

recipes.subject: the asciicast block emitter hardcodes a light-mode border colour
recipes.observed: border:1px solid #dde7e2 — a literal, whereas the sibling diagram emitter uses var(--paper-rule, #dde7e2). asciicastFigcaption likewise hardcodes color:#55635e where articleFigcaption uses var(--paper-ink-soft, #55635e). Two dark-mode defects in the asciicast path that the other block types do not have; same re-vendor as the theme fix.
